item.text:
**3B.3 Research Note: Incitement, Dehumanization, and Scapegoating**

Bottom line: **mostly negative for incitement**. I found one real but weak counterexample in Biden’s “illegal” remark about an undocumented immigrant, which he promptly regretted. Against that, there is strong 2024 evidence that he publicly denounced Islamophobia and anti-Arab hate, rejected genocidal framing, and did not use office rhetoric to personally incite violence against minorities or opponents.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Biden denounces resurgence of Islamophobia amid Gaza war | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-03-15 | https://theprint.in/world/biden-denounces-resurgence-of-islamophobia-amid-gaza-war/2002734/ | Biden condemned a rise in Islamophobia, anti-Palestinian bias, and antisemitism and said Muslims and Arabs deserve dignity and equal rights. This is direct anti-incitement evidence. | 3B.3, 3B.1 |
| Positive | White House releases strategy to counter anti-Muslim, anti-Arab hate | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-12-13 | https://theprint.in/world/white-house-releases-strategy-to-counter-anti-muslim-anti-arab-hate/2400362/ | Biden released a strategy explicitly aimed at reducing anti-Muslim and anti-Arab hate and said discrimination against whole communities is wrong. That is evidence against personal scapegoating or dehumanization. | 3B.3, 3B.1 |
| Positive | Biden: What's happening in Gaza is not genocide | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-20 | https://www.investing.com/news/politics/biden-whats-happening-in-gaza-is-not-genocide-3448942 | Biden rejected the “genocide” accusation in a pro-Israel context, but the reported framing was not a call for violence against Palestinians or other groups. It is better read as dispute over terminology than incitement. | 3B.3, 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.6 |
| Negative | Biden regrets using "illegal" to describe immigrant in speech | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-03-09 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/biden-regrets-using-illegal-to-describe-immigrant-in-speech-3331412 | Biden used a dehumanizing term for an undocumented immigrant in his State of the Union rebuttal and later said he regretted it. This is the clearest 2024 counterexample, but it was isolated and immediately walked back. | 3B.3, 3B.1 |

**Assessment**
- Strongest evidence against 3B.3: the March 2024 “illegal” comment, because it used dehumanizing language about migrants.
- Strongest evidence for 3B.3: Biden’s public anti-Islamophobia and anti-Arab statements and the White House hate-countering strategy.
- I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Biden personally incited hatred, revenge, dehumanization, or violence against journalists, civil society, religious groups, or political opponents in the way this lens defines it.

**Search gap**
- The public 2024 record I found contains **very little direct incitement-type language** from Biden himself.
- Most controversies around hate and scapegoating in 2024 were about **his opponents’ rhetoric**, not his own.
